Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

bayespk 0.2.0

  • Bug fix: with error = "log", the likelihood compared the untransformed DV with log(concentration), so log-scale fits in 0.1.0 and 0.1.1 were wrong. DV is now log-transformed. A recovery test and a simulation-based calibration scenario with log-scale error were added.
  • Data below the quantification limit: rows with CENS = 1 (DV holds the limit) are handled by Beal’s M3 method.
  • Steady state: dose records with SS = 1 and II use closed-form steady-state solutions for bolus, infusion and first-order oral doses; earlier doses are reset, and observations within one interval before the steady-state dose (troughs) are used. dose_regimen(ss = TRUE) predicts at steady state.
  • The mean/deviation split of the random effects is no longer applied to KA, which was slower without benefit in benchmarks (inst/validation/benchmark_decouple.R).

bayespk 0.1.1

  • plot() methods: individual fits on a fine time grid, observed vs predicted, trace plots, and predicted concentrations for new regimens with compare = for two regimens. All use Okabe-Ito colours.
  • predict() without regimen accepts times to return each subject’s prediction on a time grid. Predictions are returned as class bpk_prediction (a data frame).
  • prior_sensitivity() reports parameters by their names (CL, b_wt, omega_V, …).
  • New simulated data set bpk_example, used by every example.
  • Three vignettes with precomputed results and figures: getting started, covariates and informative priors, two-compartment models and regimen comparison.
  • citation("bayespk"), issue templates, and a README with figures and results.

bayespk 0.1.0

  • First release: 1- and 2-compartment linear models (IV bolus, infusion, first-order oral), closed-form solutions, log-normal between-subject variability (optionally correlated), covariate formulas, four residual error models, weakly informative default priors, diagnostics with warnings, predictions for new regimens, prior sensitivity.
  • pk_model(ka_faster = TRUE) constrains the typical KA above the disposition rate to remove flip-flop modes (off by default).
  • Random effects are sampled as a sample mean plus Helmert deviations, which removes the correlation between typical values and the mean random effect.
